additions.reason: The Torah letters are the central subject of this teaching. When gazed upon carefully, they begin to 'shine and combine' (לְהָאִיר וּלְהִצְטָרֵף). The Rebbe explicitly equates this illumination/combination to the Talmudic category of 'protruding and combining letters' (אוֹתִיּוֹת בּוֹלְטוֹת וּמִצְטָרְפוֹת) — using the word 'בִּבְחִינַת', which is the canonical bechina language. Torah letters that shine and combine ARE an aspect of / share the same nature as the miraculous protruding letters of the Urim V'Tumim. This pair (אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה ↔ אוֹתִיּוֹת בּוֹלְטוֹת) is the only bechina pair in this teaching and is not present in the dataset.
additions.source_quote: יַתְחִילוּ הָאוֹתִיּוֹת לְהָאִיר וּלְהִצְטָרֵף, בִּבְחִינַת אוֹתִיּוֹת בּוֹלְטוֹת וּמִצְטָרְפוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יומא עג:)

additions.reason: The 'protruding and combining letters' of the Urim V'Tumim (Yoma 73b) is the explicit bechina-referent of the illuminated Torah letters. In the Talmudic context, these are the letters that literally protruded from the breastplate to spell prophecy. Here the Rebbe uses this concept as the bechina-archetype for the shining/combining that Torah letters undergo when a person gazes at them with complete attention. Not in the dataset for Torah #281.
additions.source_quote: בִּבְחִינַת אוֹתִיּוֹת בּוֹלְטוֹת וּמִצְטָרְפוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יומא עג:)

additions.reason: The 'new combinations' (צֵרוּפִים חֲדָשִׁים) seen through gazing are the visible fruit of the bechina described above — the Torah letters shining and combining yield new wondrous letter-combinations. This is part of the same tight thematic cluster as אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה and אוֹתִיּוֹת בּוֹלְטוֹת: they are all aspects of the same reality of miraculous letter-illumination. The teaching says the gazer will 'see new combinations, wonders' (נִפְלָאוֹת צֵרוּפִים חֲדָשִׁים) — this is the result/expression of the same phenomenon. Not in the dataset.

analysis_notes.note_on_scope: Torah #281 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutay Moharan — three sentences presenting a single phenomenological observation about Torah-letter gazing. Its conceptual structure is correspondingly minimal: there is one bechina pair (illuminated Torah letters = protruding Urim letters) with a closely related third concept (new combinations). No packages exist in the current dataset, and the text does not support more than one thematic cluster. All three missing concepts belong to the same package domain: holy letter-illumination.
analysis_notes.note_on_adam_pashut: The 'simple person' (אָדָם פָּשׁוּט) mentioned in the text is the subject/actor, not a bechina concept. The teaching makes no 'simple person IS an aspect of X' equation. He is the one who gazes — a contextual/eitza frame, not a bechina node. Similarly, 'not putting it to the test' is practical guidance (eitza), not a bechina equivalence.
